context.body: Deuteronomy places the proposal in the people’s speech and Moses’ approval while preserving twelve representatives and good fruit.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Moses recalls arriving at the Amorite hill country, urging possession without fear, and hearing the people propose men to search the land.
observations.label: The people propose sending men ahead: action

observations.body: The proposal pleases Moses; twelve men take fruit and report that the land is good.
observations.label: The people propose sending men ahead: response

observations.body: do not fear · send men · pleased me well · twelve men · good land
observations.label: Words in Deuteronomy 1:19–25

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 1:19–25 as presumption and later retelling evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Numbers begins with the LORD telling Moses to send men; Deuteronomy begins the mission proposal with the people.
payload.title: The people propose sending men ahead
